what_changes: The business behind a store is proved with papers that differ by its country. Kuwait: a licence or commercial registration, an extract naming every beneficial owner, civil IDs and passports of owners and managers, the company's IBAN certificate (S02-SA-121). The UAE: a trade licence or registration, ownership papers where required, Emirates ID and passport for each owner, an IBAN certificate, VAT details only if registered (S02-SA-127, S02-SA-134). Salla's store country is the country where the business is registered (S02-SA-113, S02-SA-490). The entity record's fields and documents vary by country; where the country is held doesn't.
keeps_open: (b), one business per store or several; the address, map location, billing address and currency as records of their own; a display country per market (S02-D6)
closes: nothing beyond what S02-D1 already closes
evidence: S02-SA-121; S02-SA-127; S02-SA-134; S02-SA-113; S02-SA-490; c/RD1/points.tsv S02-VP-10 (Shopify's one entity form per country code: S02-SH-427, S02-SH-324)
note: Reading: one module (the entity's form and documents per country, behind S-07's checks), and a setting if the record already holds country-specific fields as data per country rather than fixed columns. Which documents is S-07's.

what_changes: Hypothesis: a seller based in Saudi Arabia serves an Egypt market through an Egyptian business of its own (whether Egypt requires that is unknown from S-02's evidence). Egypt differs on the rules that follow a business's country: Zid serves it through a separate company, Zid Egypt, with its own terms, fees in EGP with VAT, and its own privacy controller under Egypt's Law 151 of 2020 (S02-ZD-367, S02-ZD-371, S02-ZD-383, S02-ZD-384). Shopify assigns markets to business entities 'to determine payment processing and Order attribution' (S02-SH-280, S02-SH-142, S02-SH-143), and existing orders stay with the entity active when they were placed (S02-SH-147). Under D1 the second business is added and assigned to the Egypt market; rules on that market's orders must then read its country.
keeps_open: a second business per store (S02-D1); a business per market (S02-VP-63, kept open); a move by a new business (S02-D2)
note: The same finding as S02-E2's Egypt row. D1 says 'with the entity in place, a second one is a setting', but every rule reads 'the store's business-entity country' (S02-E2, S02-D3), which names one entity. Reading: with two, the rules applied to an order (payments, invoices and order attribution, the selling business's tax and checks) need the order or its market to find the right one, a change in several parts, and orders made before need their business recorded. It stays a setting if, from the start, the entry point takes the order or market and each order records its business. Shopify splits the two (reading): the store's entity serves 'financial products, markets, apps, and taxes' (S02-SH-318) and subscriptions (S02-SH-1146), a market's entity payment processing and order attribution (S02-SH-280).

what_changes: Assumption: 'the company' is Sharrwah's own (PLAN.md section 6, step 0, uses the word so). With Sharrwah based in Oman or Egypt, or contracting through a company per region as Zid does (its Saudi company, S02-ZD-003; Zid Egypt, S02-ZD-367; Zid Syria, S02-ZD-140) and as Shopify and BigCommerce do by the merchant's billing address or residence (S02-SH-001, S02-SH-003, S02-BC-151, S02-BC-066), what changes is the Sharrwah company, law, fee tax and privacy controller each seller country maps to. Where the seller's country is held doesn't change.
keeps_open: everything D1 keeps; one Sharrwah company for every seller, or one per seller country (S02-E2: one value, or a value per country)
note: The values are S-03's, S-05's and S-08's. The seller's business record doesn't depend on where Sharrwah is based.

what_changes: The first market leaves the launch, or Sharrwah stops serving it later. D1 names no market and was made from the five references alone (decisions.md, opening), so only values change: whether a business record may hold that country (S-07's one list) and, for stores already there, a move (S02-D2) or a closure (S-03).
note: 'One entity per store at launch' is a starting configuration the model goes beyond, not a limit set by today's capacity, so it isn't flagged.

what_changes: Where a platform holds a balance for the seller, a move waits for it: Zid makes a store's country change wait until the wallet balance is brought to zero, and a balance that can't be zeroed goes to customer service (S02-ZD-055, S02-ZD-056; for Gulf merchants, S02-ZD-173); its wallet amounts in OMR, AED, KWD and BHD can't be withdrawn (S02-ZD-114). Under Decision 1 no such balance exists at launch (S02-R4); one would exist in a market where the founder later lets Sharrwah or a partner hold money.
keeps_open: (b)'s conditions, run as checks before the switch; (c); (d) for staff where a contract or several businesses bind it; (a) for a display default country (S02-D6)
closes: (a) for the legal country: changing it in place
reason: an engineering cost greater than the option's value (rules and records keyed on the country would change meaning silently); a confirmed fact (Shopify and WooPayments lock it: S02-SH-596, S02-WC-182)
evidence: S02-ZD-055; S02-ZD-056; S02-ZD-173; S02-ZD-114; S02-SH-596; S02-WC-182; c/RD1/answers.tsv S02-VP-07; register S02-F3
note: One module: a balance check from the holder's ledger joins the checks D2 already runs behind one interface. The register keeps 'whether a balance must be cleared before a move' open (S02-F3); this is where it lands.

what_changes: If Sharrwah's company, law or fee tax differ by the seller's country, as Zid's do between zid.sa and zid.eg (S02-ZD-003, S02-ZD-367, S02-ZD-371), a move also changes the seller's contract with Sharrwah and the tax on Sharrwah's fees. Reading: with Sharrwah in Egypt, a seller moving into or out of Egypt turns from a foreign customer of Sharrwah into a domestic one, or back; the tax effect is S-05's and unknown here.
note: D2 already runs other subjects' checks before the switch (the contract, S-03; tax forms, S-05); the new country's values fill them.

what_changes: Sellers whose business record is in the dropped country move (D2's procedure: a new record in the new country, the old one closed once nothing open rests on it) or close (S-03). The procedure names no country.
note: D2's trade-off, that records made under the old country keep their meaning, is what keeps a dropped market's orders and invoices readable.

what_changes: A service open by where the store or its stock is, not where the business is registered: Zid's Jahez needs 'the store's or the stock's location in one of the Kingdom's cities' (S02-ZD-120, S02-V-186, phase B's translation); its other conditions (a commercial registration or a freelance document, Mazeed, quick-to-prepare products) name no country. Hypothesis: a business registered in the UAE with stock in Riyadh meets Zid's condition, but D3's key, the business's country, says it doesn't.
keeps_open: (a) to (d) and (f), joined in the business's country; (e) as one value for every country
closes: a rule keyed on the store's or the stock's location
reason: none of the three: the reason given ('two countries for one seller can disagree') is argued for a second record of the seller's own country (the billing address, a feature's field); a stock location is a different fact, which it doesn't weigh
evidence: S02-ZD-120; S02-V-186; c/RD1/points.tsv S02-VP-17 (Zid's Jahez per the store's location); register S02-D3 (closes)
note: One module: the rule reads the stock location (a record of its own under S02-D1; stock locations are a per-market setting under S02-D6), as D3's own cost_later allows ('one rule's own key'). S02-E2 carries the same closure. Narrowing it to second records of the seller's own country would keep this option.

what_changes: A check keyed on a person's country beside the business's: Salla's UAE verification asks an Emirates ID and a passport for each owner 'If you are a UAE resident; if not use a national ID from the country you reside in' (S02-SA-134, S02-V-154). And, on BigCommerce's own markets, a payment method keyed on the provider account's and the shopper's countries beside the store's: Fastlane by PayPal (S02-BC-128, S02-V-230); BigCommerce Payments needs a UK or US-based PayPal Business account (S02-BC-081, S02-V-228). D3 reads only the business's country.
closes: rules keyed on an owner's residence, or on a provider account's country
reason: none of the three: an owner's residence is a fact about a person, not a second record of the seller's country; under Decision 1 a provider account is the seller's own with the provider (S02-R4), and its country is the provider's record, not one Sharrwah keeps
note: One module each: S-07's checks read the owners' records; S-04's rules read the provider account. The register itself uses a provider account's scope: S02-E5's payment methods choose 'among the seller's provider accounts allowed there', which D3's closure as worded forbids.

what_changes: The values behind the one entry point change per seller country (Sharrwah's company and law, the tax on its fees, the privacy controller); the key doesn't. Zid Egypt's plans are paid in EGP and subject to VAT (S02-ZD-371); on one Zid development store a plan's invoice carried a VAT line in EGP, and in AED a VAT of 0 (S02-ZD-476, S02-ZD-477), which phase C reads as Zid's fee VAT following the store's business-address country (c/RD1/points.tsv S02-VP-15, a reading).
keeps_open: 'every store alike' as one value; a value per country
note: Reading: a fee's tax may depend on the pair (Sharrwah's company's country, the seller's country); with one Sharrwah company, or one chosen by the seller's country, the pair follows from the seller's country, so it stays a value per country.

what_changes: The rules' values for the dropped country go unused; the entry point and its key stay.

As S02-D1's Egypt row. A seller with one business in Egypt is a setting: Egypt's values (Zid Egypt's company, terms, EGP fees with VAT and privacy controller show how they differ: S02-ZD-367, S02-ZD-371, S02-ZD-383, S02-ZD-384) fill the table. The test is a store that adds an Egyptian business for its Egypt market (hypothesis), as Shopify allows (S02-SH-142, S02-SH-143, S02-SH-280). E2 reads every seller-country rule 'through one interface keyed on the store's business-entity country'.
keeps_open: every binding as a value per seller country, or one value for all
note: Keyed on the store, the interface can't tell which business an order belongs to; adding the order or market later changes every part that calls it for an order, and orders already made need their business. Reading: it is kept a setting by stating now that (1) the entry point takes the order or market as well as the store, (2) each order records the business active when it was placed (Shopify: S02-SH-147), (3) each rule says whether it reads the store's main business or the order's. S02-E5 already resolves per market ('where an entity is assigned to a market ... that entity's arrangement applies'), so E2 and E5 disagree on the key as worded.

what_changes: The table behind the interface changes: which Sharrwah company contracts with each seller country, its law, the tax on its fees, the privacy controller, and the countries kept out. The references' kept-out lists follow their own jurisdictions (comprehensive US sanctions: S02-BC-073, S02-WC-079; Shopify's list: S02-SH-273); an Omani or Egyptian company's list is unknown from S-02's evidence.
keeps_open: one value for all, or a value per seller country, per binding
note: The values are S-03's, S-05's, S-07's and S-08's.

what_changes: Hypothesis: the company's country (Egypt, say), or a seller's, requires data to be held in that country. Shopify keeps new European merchants' 'store data, order data and customer personal data stored at rest in Europe by default' (S02-SH-625) and applies data protection laws 'based on the location or residence of Merchant and/or Your Customer(s)' (S02-SH-621); Zid Egypt's policy is issued under Egypt's Law 151 of 2020 (S02-ZD-384), whose storage rules are unknown from S-02's evidence.
note: Where data is stored isn't a value a rule reads, so E2's one interface doesn't reach it: meeting it changes storage. No S-02 option causes or avoids this; it is S-08's to settle before storage is designed. The same holds for a second market whose law requires it.

what_changes: That country's values go unused; the interface and its key stay.

Who holds an order's money can follow the market sold into: Salla shows cash on delivery, where the courier holds the money, only in Saudi Arabia and hides it in other markets automatically (S02-SA-283); Zid gives no cash on delivery on international shipping (S02-ZD-129); Shopify selects its Managed Markets merchant of record automatically for a customer shipping to a managed market (S02-SH-541). E5 keys the arrangement on the seller's business, each market's payment methods choosing among the seller's accounts.
keeps_open: C everywhere; A or B per seller's country, if the founder allows them; a business's arrangement per market (S02-VP-63)
closes: the market sold into as the key of the holding arrangement, apart from a business
reason: a confirmed fact: providers, and the platforms' own payment services, take on a seller by its country (the merchant's country, a commonality for S02-VP-11 and S02-VP-12)
evidence: S02-SA-283; S02-ZD-129; S02-ZD-127; S02-SH-541; c/RD1/answers.tsv S02-VP-11, S02-VP-12; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-62, S02-VP-64; register S02-R4, S02-R5
note: Cash on delivery per market is already a payment-method setting (S02-D6): a setting. A merchant of record per market (S-03's; a per-market setting in decisions.md) holds that market's orders' money whatever the seller's country: E5's resolver lets it take precedence, one module, given the resolver takes the order's market, as E5 already does for a business per market. Whether a merchant of record counts under Decision 1 is S-01's and S-03's, unknown here. E5 is engineering's reading of the founder's 'a market's setting' (26 October), which S02-R5 leaves S-02 to place; the founder confirms it.

what_changes: Hypothesis: if the founder later lets Sharrwah hold money (A) only where its company is licensed, say Oman, the arrangement differs by the seller's country: A for sellers in Oman, C elsewhere. Reading: the references show a platform's own holding tied to its home regulator and limited abroad: Salla's transfers fall under the Saudi Central Bank's authority (S02-SA-211); Zid's wallet amounts in OMR, AED, KWD and BHD can't be withdrawn by its merchants outside Saudi Arabia (S02-ZD-114).
keeps_open: A or B per seller's country; C everywhere
evidence: S02-SA-211; S02-ZD-114; register S02-R4, S02-R6, S02-E5
note: Under the guard, nothing that holds sellers' money through Sharrwah goes live without the founder's decision (S02-R6).

what_changes: C everywhere at launch is the founder's Decision 1 for every market (S02-R4), not tied to the first; nothing changes.

Saudi Arabia shows market kinds beyond places: Zid's sales-channel marketplaces as markets (Amazon, Trendyol, Jahez, Mazeed: S02-ZD-146), Salla's point-of-sale market (Salla Point, S02-SA-180; for stores in Saudi Arabia only, S02-SA-169) and city markets (S02-SA-051); under app design, Salla says 'The Multi-Market feature is currently available only for stores in Saudi Arabia' (S02-SA-280). A second market differs in which kinds its sellers need; that Salla's limits are today's, not a market's rule, is a reading.
keeps_open: (a), (b) and (c): places first, then channel, point-of-sale, business-customer and storefront kinds; a market within a market
closes: (d): channels, points of sale and customer groups as mechanisms apart from markets
reason: an engineering cost greater than the option's value: two mechanisms would answer which values a buyer sees (S02-SH-117, S02-SH-604)
note: One module per new kind, as D4 states, on a condition (reading): matching takes a buyer context (country, city, channel, location, company) from the start, even while only places are filled; a matcher fed the buyer's country alone would make each kind a change wherever a buyer is placed. Shopify, whose (c) D4 adopts, keeps a customer-segment discount apart from markets, for all of them (S02-SH-198); the cost judgment behind closing (d) doesn't weigh it (S02-D6's first row).

what_changes: Nothing in what a market can be depends on where Sharrwah's company is. Which countries a market may hold follows S-07's list (S02-M4), whose values may follow the company's jurisdiction, as the references' kept-out lists follow theirs (S02-BC-073, S02-WC-079).
Markets holding the dropped country lose it, a value of S-07's list; what a market can be doesn't change.

Salla holds one country per market because 'Taxes are calculated based on the country assigned to each market' (S02-SA-077); its use case is a store selling in the UAE and Saudi Arabia that shows UAE tax to UAE customers and Saudi tax to Saudi customers (S02-SA-105). A seller wants one GCC market, each buyer taxed by their own country.
keeps_open: one country per market, as a configuration; several countries per market; a country in markets of different kinds; the seller limiting who enters a market
closes: one country per market as a rule of the model; two markets of one kind claiming a buyer
reason: a confirmed fact for the first: tax follows the buyer's country on all five (c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-57|the buyer's country, a commonality); an engineering cost greater than the option's value for the second (nothing orders two markets of one kind)
note: Tax by each buyer's country inside one market is S-05's, read per buyer. WooCommerce can also tax from the shop's base address (S02-WC-206), one value for every buyer, which a multi-country market also meets.

what_changes: Placement and overlap don't depend on where Sharrwah's company is.
Markets holding the dropped country lose it; the placement rules stay.

A store's own country and its main market can differ: on Zid's development store the business address was changed to Kuwait while, by phase C's reading, the primary market's countries stayed Saudi Arabia (S02-ZD-467, S02-ZD-468, S02-ZD-471; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-85). Shopify's primary market is one country or region, can't be deleted, and follows the store currency (S02-SH-128); the last region market can't be deleted, disabled or retyped (S02-SH-287).
keeps_open: a main market whose places differ from the business's country; any places for it
reason: a confirmed fact: every reference has a default market (c/RD2/answers.tsv S02-VP-26|a default market, a commonality)
evidence: S02-ZD-467; S02-ZD-468; S02-ZD-471; S02-SH-128; S02-SH-287; c/RD2/answers.tsv S02-VP-26; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-85
note: E3 doesn't tie the main market to the business's country, and shouldn't. It doesn't say whether the main market's places may change, which the first-market-dropped row needs (Shopify: 'Change your primary market', S02-SH-128).

what_changes: A store's main market doesn't depend on where Sharrwah's company is.
Stores whose main market holds the dropped country keep a main market, which can't be removed (E3; Shopify, S02-SH-128), so its places change to another country.
note: A setting only if the main market's places may change; E3 should say so.

what_changes: Hypothesis: a buyer matches markets of two kinds, such as a business customer in a country market (S-02's evidence shows no founder market with business-customer markets). Shopify applies the more specific type's customizations, but 'Catalogs from all applicable markets are combined, so customers can access products from all relevant catalogs' (S02-SH-109), and a customer-segment discount 'applies to all markets' (S02-SH-198). Under D6 the most specific value wins, from the one market S02-D5 places the buyer in.
keeps_open: the most specific value winning; a market within a market; a product's restriction
closes: combining a setting's values across the markets a buyer matches (products offered, discounts)
reason: none of the three: D6 states 'Nothing a reference shows is closed', which S02-SH-109 contradicts for catalogs
evidence: S02-SH-109; S02-SH-198; register S02-D6 (closes), S02-D5, S02-E1; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-47, S02-VP-51
note: One module (reading): the resolver (S02-E1) can find every market a buyer matches from their conditions and combine a set-valued setting, while the order still records one market. Per-setting precedence across the matched markets, as Shopify's 'for how your market customizations take effect' reads, fits the same module.

what_changes: No per-market setting depends on where Sharrwah's company is; a closure of a store by Sharrwah, which ranks above the seller's store status, follows S-03's terms (decisions.md, the S-03 row).
evidence: decisions.md (What moved to other subjects); register S02-M1

what_changes: Values set for markets holding the dropped country go unused.

A Saudi store sells into Kuwait in KWD: Zid's development store held a Kuwait market in KWD beside a Saudi main market in SAR (S02-ZD-467, its scope); a UAE store's own currency is AED (S02-SA-501). A provider may also convert at payment: with Stripe Adaptive Pricing 'shoppers can complete orders in their local currency, while payouts to your account are settled in your default currency' (S02-BC-224); who converts is S-04's.
keeps_open: (a), (b), (c); (d) as a market within a market; one currency per store, every market inheriting it
closes: money records that keep one currency only
reason: an engineering cost greater than the option's value (a second amount costs little now and a redesign later)
note: A setting for the market's currency and prices. Reading: a provider's conversion puts a third currency on the payment; that stays one module (the payment record) if each amount carries its own currency code, so D7's 'both amounts' shouldn't be built as two fixed columns. Shopify's duty-inclusive prices need local currencies at a guaranteed rate, not a manual one (S02-SH-531), a rule D7's rate setting must allow. Whether a market's currency needs a precision the store's lacks is unknown from S-02's evidence.

what_changes: Sharrwah's own billing currency changes; it is S-09's and sits on Sharrwah's billing record, not on markets. Salla bills all fees in SAR (S02-SA-208), Zid in SAR or the merchant's local currency (S02-ZD-057), Zid Egypt in EGP (S02-ZD-371). Markets' currencies don't change.
Markets' currencies are values; a store whose own currency changes after a move is S02-E4's row.

Some per-market values are set by the platform or by a law, not by the seller: Salla shows cash on delivery only in Saudi Arabia and hides it in other markets automatically (S02-SA-283); Zid gives none on international shipping and lets some couriers offer it on local shipping for a 10-riyal fee (S02-ZD-129, S02-ZD-127); a store sending marketing messages to the UK must comply with the UK's PECR (S02-SH-954; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-82). E1's chain holds only the seller's values: a product's, then the market's, then the store's.
keeps_open: a value per market for every listed setting; a product's narrower shipping and payment methods; a value held once for the store
closes: nothing (E1 doesn't rule the layer out; it doesn't name it)
evidence: S02-SA-283; S02-ZD-129; S02-ZD-127; S02-SH-954; c/RD3/answers.tsv S02-VP-62, S02-VP-82; register S02-F8
note: One module: a rule layer in the one resolver, keyed on the buyer's country or market, limits what a seller's value may be. The register already sets returns, messages and the address form per market by a named rule or a regional pattern (decisions.md, RD3); this is the layer they need.

what_changes: How a per-market setting is read doesn't depend on where Sharrwah's company is.
No change to how a setting is read.

Payouts follow the payment account's country and currency: Salla pays UAE stores weekly above AED 250 and Kuwait stores daily with a KWD 1 minimum (S02-SA-145, S02-SA-150); on Shopify each entity's account has its own payout currency, the conversion fee depending on which entity processes the payment (S02-SH-183), and Advanced and Plus stores may add a payout account in a non-domestic currency (S02-SH-035). A store with a Saudi and a UAE business (D1's room) is paid out in SAR and AED; E4 makes the store's one currency the payout currency, and the gift cards'.
keeps_open: one store currency for the store's own reports and as every market's starting currency (S02-D7)
closes: payouts in a currency per business or provider account; gift cards in a market's currency
reason: none of the three: Shopify's gift cards (S02-SH-189) and BigCommerce's Stripe payouts (S02-BC-224) are two vendors' choices, and Shopify itself pays out in several currencies (S02-SH-035, S02-SH-183); under Decision 1 a payout is the provider's, into the seller's own account (S02-R4), not Sharrwah's to set
note: One module each: payout records carry their own currency in the holder's ledger, a separate part (S01-E2, through S02-R5); gift-card balances carry theirs. Shopify tells multi-entity sellers using some apps to 'Manually reconcile your payouts' (S02-SH-1149). S02-D7 repeats the clause ('which stays the currency of gift cards and payouts').

what_changes: The store's own currency is the seller's; Sharrwah's billing currency is S-09's, on Sharrwah's billing record.

A seller in the dropped market who moves (S02-D2) may change the store's own currency to the new country's. Shopify sets the store currency from the business country (S02-SH-883) and says changing the store's country 'might affect' the 'local language and currency for your store' (S02-SH-248). E4 keeps one store currency but doesn't say whether it may change.
note: Reading: a setting if every record's store amount carries its currency code, so amounts made before the change keep their meaning; if records assume one store currency that never changes, a change is a redesign. Stating it now costs nothing.
